html:
Guyana is an English-speaking country on the northern coast of South America, between Venezuela and Suriname. It was the colony of British Guiana until independence in 1966, and the map shows it under the name Guyana from 1914.

In the colonial years sugar ruled the coast. After slavery ended, planters brought indentured workers from India, and by the 1900s Indo-Guyanese were the largest group, with Afro-Guyanese the second.

Politics split along those lines:

  • Cheddi Jagan and his People's Progressive Party won the first elections under universal suffrage in 1953. Britain feared communism and suspended the constitution after 133 days.
  • His party split, and Forbes Burnham built a rival party with mostly Afro-Guyanese support. With British and American backing, Burnham led the country to independence in 1966 and ruled until his death in 1985.
  • In 1978 over nine hundred members of an American cult died at Jonestown in the Guyanese jungle.
  • Jagan returned to power in free elections in 1992.

Venezuela claims the Essequibo region, about two thirds of Guyana's land. In 2015 ExxonMobil found large oil fields offshore, and since production began in 2019 Guyana's economy has grown faster than almost any other in the world. Its neighbour Suriname shares a similar colonial past under the Dutch.
sum: Guyana is an English-speaking country on the northern coast of South America, between Venezuela and Suriname. It was the colony of British Guiana until independence in 1966, and the map shows it under the name Guyana from 1914.
